evidence.notes: The listed short common adjectives (long, beau, nouveau, bon, mauvais, vieux, jeune) are placed before the noun; examples use each listed adjective.

proposals.entity_key: Some irregular passé simple stems based on past participle

evidence.notes: Several irregular passé simple stems resemble the past participle, but the resemblance is not a fixed rule, so the examples are illustrative only.

value: fou -> fol, vieux -> vieil, nouveau -> nouvel, beau -> bel

evidence.notes: These adjectives take a special masculine singular form before a noun beginning with a vowel sound, as stated in the rule formation.
The c of -cer verbs takes a cedilla before o to keep the soft /s/ sound, as in the nous form of the listed verb prononcer.

value: acheter -> j'achète, tu achètes, il achète, ils achètent
e -> è in all but nous and vous

evidence.notes: The silent e of the stem becomes è in every form except nous and vous, matching the rule formation for acheter.

value: épeler -> j'épelle, tu épelles, il épelle, ils épellent

evidence.notes: The l is doubled in all forms except nous and vous, as in the rule formation for épeler; appeler follows the same pattern.
The g of -ger verbs takes an e before o to keep the soft /ʒ/ sound, as in the nous form of the listed verb voyager.

value: répéter -> je répète, tu répètes, il répète, ils répètent
é -> è in all but nous and vous

evidence.notes: The é of the stem becomes è in every form except nous and vous, matching the rule formation for répéter.

proposals.entity_key: Spelling changes for -cer and -ger verbs in passé simple
value: commencer -> je commençai, nous commençâmes, ils commencèrent
manger -> je mangeai, nous mangeâmes, ils mangèrent

evidence.notes: When the passé simple ending begins with -a, -cer verbs use a cedilla and -ger verbs add an extra -e-, as shown with commencer and manger.
The future stem shows the same spelling modifications throughout all persons; note that préférer keeps é in the future and conditional, unlike the present.
